content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware geocoding and spatial modelling link partially located farm policies to hail exposure estimates and identify potentially underpriced portfolio segments more reliably than municipality-level loading? The first experiment would mask known policy coordinates to settlement level, test whether methods transferred from health registries recover useful exposure estimates, and compare held-out loss predictions while explicitly testing the limits of five-kilometre daily weather data.

rationale.text: Pejić has directly relevant experience adapting spatial smoothing to incomplete addresses in administrative insurance claims, although in health rather than agricultural insurance.

sources.quote: adapting registry-based spatial smoothing approaches to the fund's incomplete address fields.

rationale.text: His hierarchical geographic imputation methods address the company's settlement-only location problem and have an R implementation validated on real Vojvodina registry data.

sources.quote: a missing street address is known to lie within a settlement, which lies within a municipality.
The procedure was implemented in R and validated on the Vojvodina CRC registry

rationale.text: He has evaluated Serbian address-geocoding methods against field-verified coordinates, providing relevant experience for measuring rural location uncertainty rather than treating matches as exact.

sources.quote: The ensemble approach also produced positional accuracy estimates; median offset from field-verified coordinates was 148 m for urban addresses and 540 m for rural addresses.

rationale.text: His work provides a precedent for masked-location validation and evaluating both prediction error and uncertainty coverage.

sources.quote: A random 30% of geocoded cases were masked to simulate the incomplete-geocoding scenario.
Predictive performance was evaluated by mean absolute error and interval coverage at tract level.

constraints.text: Field-level exposure must not be presented as directly observed: settlement-only policy locations and five-kilometre daily weather inputs impose spatial and temporal limits that the feasibility experiment must quantify.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: Validation must work within the reported three-year, approximately 1,200-policy dataset and use real location references; confirm that loss coordinates identify insured assets before using them as geocoding ground truth.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.
He has expressed preference for partners who can supply real address or location data for validation work rather than purely synthetic datasets.

constraints.text: Any operational output must feed the existing Python quarterly pricing workflow rather than remain a standalone map; an integration owner is needed given the company's shared operational staffing.

sources.quote: Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh
a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.

constraints.text: The initial scope and schedule must accommodate limited supervisory capacity before mid-2027; actual availability remains unconfirmed.

sources.quote: which limits capacity for large new commitments before mid-2027.

risks: The demonstrated methods concern residential cancer records and relatively smooth incidence surfaces, not farm parcels, narrow hail tracks or insured loss severity. Population-weighted allocation and spatial smoothing could misplace agricultural exposure or blur storm boundaries; the first masked-coordinate experiment must test this transfer.

Daily five-kilometre weather grids may not contain enough information to identify field-level hail intensity. Better geocoding alone cannot recover unobserved storm detail, and finer-resolution weather observations may be needed.

Three claim years may represent too few independent storms for stable validation. Geo-tagged losses alone may also give a biased view of exposure if non-claiming policies and coverage histories are unavailable.
The reported 18% excess does not establish exposure misclassification as its cause; repair inflation, coverage mix, deductibles or claims practices could also explain the gap.

Researcher availability, budget, deadline, data-access permissions and operational ownership are unknown. His stated joint-project interest concerns spatial health analysis, so willingness to undertake agricultural insurance work needs confirmation.
Operational adoption could fail despite a successful prototype: the company's earlier flood-risk mapping collaboration was completed but has not been integrated into pricing.
questions: Will Pejić undertake a bounded agricultural-insurance joint project, and what time can he and his team commit before and after mid-2027?
Do the available records include all insured farms, including those without claims, with coverage periods, sums insured, deductibles, premiums, asset type and dated claim amounts?

What do the loss coordinates represent: damaged fields or buildings, farm residences, settlement centroids or assessor locations? Can parcel boundaries or independently verified asset coordinates be obtained for validation?

Which hail-related variables, timestamps, uncertainty estimates and historical revisions does MeteoVoj supply, and can radar, hail reports or finer-resolution observations be licensed if the existing grid proves insufficient?
What budget, delivery deadline, data-protection arrangements and weather-data usage rights apply, and who will own the R-to-Python integration and ongoing maintenance?

Can the first experiment reserve whole storms or years for evaluation, compare against municipality loading, and agree acceptable location error, exposure uncertainty and held-out loss calibration before any pricing deployment?
